body.text: Original Report
Huaishu: the effects last so long! There's still an aftereffect now. [18:39]
Huaishu: Pochi, I o'd heavy last night, and I remembered a lot of how the outside world felt when I was little... does this count as part of dissociation? [06:12]
Gotō: hold on, tell me in detail.

Huaishu: I remembered a lot of things from when I was little, the scenery or the smells of childhood, like the dreamcore stuff on short-video apps, and things I gradually forgot in recent years; right now the painful, even traumatic things aren't what comes up for me.
Gotō: what did you take?
Huaishu: the dispersible dextro tablets, swallowed with cola. In the morning I'd taken fluoxetine, tandospirone, trihexyphenidyl.
Huaishu: it feels like I went and had that electroshock therapy, what's it called.

Huaishu: worth mentioning, I remembered the angle and the method I used to look at the world and at things when I was little. Since the depression, I'd forgotten a lot of how I understood the world as a child. Now that so much is back, I feel like my personality has become more outgoing.

Huaishu: like some childhood quirks — thinking some people were squares and some were circles, having to step up stairs right foot first. I'm Asperger's myself, so what I feel may be different from other people.
Huaishu: I remembered what my childhood friends looked like, some people and things I'd forgotten.
Gotō: does this feeling — do you find it comfortable? Or, does it come with an antidepressant effect?
Huaishu: I feel very good about myself. I think it does.

Huaishu: recalling childhood memories filled in what I lacked in my understanding of the world before adulthood (maybe some trauma made me forget things). I could use my present thinking to feed back into my past wounds. In another sense, I grew up all over again.
Gotō: this person, could you keep trying... just like this, keep trying trihexyphenidyl plus Umi. And the cola might be a key factor.
Huaishu: sure, no problem.
Huaishu: so I think it really does have an antidepressant effect, not necessarily physiological — psychological.
Huaishu: the od was around three in the afternoon; I'd eaten at noon, about seventy percent full.
Gotō: hey wait, how's your memory now, any forgetfulness?
Huaishu: it's gotten worse. Sure. But I've always had too good a memory.
Gotō: isn't that strange — you can recall the past, but the present is hard to recall.
Huaishu: yes! I'd rather recall the pure, bright times of the past.
Huaishu: because, fuck, there's a wall between me now and me as a kid [a wall = no depersonalization]. After od-ing, it's gone. I know who I am; I've integrated my social image.
Huaishu: I have some pre-schizophrenia signs, like auditory and visual hallucinations.
Huaishu: before I od, when I fell asleep I'd always end up replaying painful memories for no reason.
Huaishu: true, my traumatic events seem to be covered over. I don't know how long it'll last?

Huaishu: the second or third day, taking dextromethorphan plus trihexyphenidyl like that, it really brought back a lot of my lost memories and courage. Like you said, I remembered what a happy person I used to be.
Huaishu: it came walking toward me almost glowing. It felt like being hugged. The child I was and the adult I am really came together.
Huaishu: I'd say this effect goes far beyond dissociation and hallucination. It's a pure feeling of happiness.
Handler's Note

No. 20 is corroboration for the afterglow, not a reproduction. Huaishu's experience resembles Gotō's RP-7-12, but his drug combination, constitution and context are all different. Here Gotō realised for the first time: the afterglow might not be his hallucination alone.
The original contained specific quantities and weight conversions; they have been blacked out.
